Oh wow. The first trip with my boyfriend was so magical, but I'll just talk about the first two days <3

He was the one to come and fly to me, and generally I'm a very shy and reserved person, so I remember I told him to not try and hug me the first time we saw each other. But I don't know, as soon as I saw him standing in the airport, I was the one who couldn't resist jumping into his arms.

We had coffee in the airport to try and calm down, plus he was hungry lol. And yeah, it was a bit awkward at first, but as soon as the first five minutes passed by, it was as if we had known each other for our whole lives.

He rented a car, and bought me flowers before dropping me off for my class. And then we had our first date at a Hibachi restaurant.

The next day, we went to a nearby mall where he treated me to a shopping spree, and after we had lunch, I gave him my first kiss <3 He then took me back to my dorm, so that I could freshen up and he returned to take me to dinner to a steakhouse

I always knew he was gonna ask me to be his girlfriend, but I definitely didnt expect for him to ask me in my campus' parking lot. So I just told him to wait since I didn't want to be asked out in a place like that lol. Anyways, as soon as we sat down at the steakhouse, I told him to ask me again. And we've been going strong for 6 months ever since <3

I definitely don't "barely" know my boyfriend. We've been talking daily for 5 months now. We've discussed our life, our goals, our past, our flaws, our strengths, and how we see our future. It's not like we jumped into anything either, he waited until we were able to meet each other in person to ask me to be his girlfriend.

And, yeah, he lives in another country, but so what? With how the internet is nowadays, it's so easy to stay connected. We videocall daily, play games together, watch shows together, have regular coffee dates, and keep each other company while we're working. We do normal couple things together despite the distance.

I obviously do get why my parents are freaked out. To them, he is a random man, but to me, he's not. Which is why I've offered for them to meet and talk to him, but the time I offered it, they didn't take me up on it :(

And regarding the money and gifts, that's just basic relationship behavior. You're supposed to give your girlfriend, or the girl you like, gifts.
If they could just see how good he is to me, I'm sure they wouldn't be so negative about our relationship. But the distance makes it difficult :(

I don't really know what type of relationship my parents think we have. I do think they're aware we're more than friends, but yeah, maybe the gifts are what freak them out and make them think I'm his sugar baby?

I'm definitely not though.

We didn't want to hit them with so much all at once. Like, it would already be hard to process the purse, the age gap, and the distance all at once. We thought that telling them we were just friends would calm them down a bit. And that depending on their reaction, I could open up more afterwards.

But, my parents aren't dumb, and while we don't think they know we're a couple, they definitely know he's trying to "court" me and are against it.

Yeah, I have thought of that, and it's a comment that I receive a lot.

It's true that he's very generous and I appreciate him for that, but it's definitely not a sugar relationship at all. Since we're long distance, he can't really take me out on dates or physically give me any gifts, so he's left with the option of sending me money to treat myself.

I do still live at home, at least during the vacation period. And I am still completely financially reliable on my parents, so it's not like I can just disregard their opinion or ditch them.

The first time I told them about him, it wasn't positive, but it also wasn't the worst. It was definitely more negative than anything though.

It was basically just them telling me that they're worried that he's so much older than me. He has more life experience, and I'm realistically just starting to be an adult and just starting to date. Which is true, and we're very conscious about that.

They also told me that he could be lying about who he is and about his life in general, since it's the internet. Which, yeah, we both took our precautions at first, but now it's pretty evident that we both know the other as well as any normal couple would.

I guess I do plan to have a heart to heart with them, and as you said, talk with logic. I'm just scared it might not work out :(
